newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Bacob in first Belgian mortgage-backed bond deal.
newsitem.headline: Bacob in first Belgian mortgage-backed bond deal.

text.p: Belgium's first mortgage-backed securities will be launched at the end of this month with a 9.5 billion Belgian franc deal by Bacob, the country's seventh largest bank, Bacob said.

Bacob will sell mortgages worth about 9.5 billion francs in all to an independent issuer - MBS-1 - formed by Lessius NV and Swiss Life Belgium, which in turn issues the securities to finance the purchase.
The bonds have a floating rate -- three-month Bibor plus a margin -- and a quarterly coupon. Each security note has a minimum denomination of five million francs.
The prospectus will be available from January 30 when the margins will be fixed. These will reflect the risk premium and lack of liquidity compared to state issues.

Pricing is on February 4 when the offer opens for subscriptions until February 17 inclusive. The Bibor rate will be fixed on February 20, and the securities will be quoted on the Brussels stock exchange from February 25.
Three tranches will be issued for which Bacob expects an Aaa rating from Moody's Investment Services and an AAA rating from Fitch Investors Service.
A fourth tranche with an expected A3 Moody's rating and Fitch A rating will also be launched.

Bacob Chairman Dirk Bruneel said mortgage-backed securities meant a bank could make its loans liquid, manage its capital more effectively, offer long-term fixed rate mortgages and provide more variety for investors.
Bruneel said such bonds were "important for Belgium as a financial centre", and he encouraged competition. "We don't want to remain the only ones in this market," he said.

Securitisation enables a bank, government authority or company to convert non-tradeable assets - such a cash flows from car loans, mortgages or consumer credits - into tradeable securities which can be offered to investors.
The practice is well established in the United States, and markets for securitised products have been developed in Europe since 1987.
Bacob, which last April launched Belgium's first asset backed securities, will act as market maker for the new mortgage-backed bonds which are aimed at institutional investors.

The mortgages backing the securities are 10 to 20 year residential housing loans granted by Bacob since January 1, 1995 which have fixed interest rates of between 7.5 and 10 percent. They represent about 10 percent of all Bacob's mortgage loans.

Bacob said 92 percent of the loans were for a first residence which was owner-occupied, with the homes spread out across Belgium. The average loan amount was about two million francs, with the largest totalling about seven million.
The weighted average coupon would be 8.28 percent - with the maximum at 10 percent, Bacob said.

The management company is TBE, the only one licensed by Belgium's Banking and Finance Commission for securitisation transactions. TBE is a joint venture between Bacob, Banque Bruxelles Lambert (BBL), Generale Bank and Bear Stearns of the United States.
Clearing is through the Belgian National Bank, Cedel and Euroclear.
